profile.reading:
Sabey Data Centers operates SDC Columbia, a data center campus at 4405 Grant Road in East Wenatchee, Douglas County, Washington, in the Columbia River region. Sabey traces its roots to 1972, when Dave Sabey founded Sabey Corporation as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer; the company entered the data center business almost by accident during the dot-com collapse, when a vacated tenant building in Seattle became SDC Seattle Building 5. Sabey Data Centers itself was formally established in 2010 as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors, a structure confirmed on both the operator's own site and independently by Wikipedia. As of 2026 Sabey operates seven data center campuses nationally, together totaling more than 3.5 million square feet and, per Wikipedia's most recent figure, nearly 400 MW of capacity; Tim Mirick became Sabey's president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood.

Per the operator's own SDC Columbia page, the East Wenatchee campus is marketed on renewable hydroelectric power priced at 5 cents per kilowatt-hour, drawn from the Columbia River hydroelectric system that also supplies neighboring Quincy, Washington's data center cluster. The campus comprises three completed buildings plus a fourth under construction, totaling roughly 70 MW of capacity campus-wide, a figure the operator does not break out per individual building. Aggregator Baxtel separately reports an additional 9 MW of Tier III-standard critical power expected at the campus from Q4 2026, a forward-looking figure not yet delivered as of this writing and not applied as confirmed capacity to any building here.

This specific building, Intergate Columbia A, carries no separately confirmed street number distinct from Buildings B and D in sourcing located to date, unlike its two neighbors which aggregator DatacenterHawk lists individually; the shared campus address from the operator's own page is applied here instead.
profile.capacity_note: not published at the building level. Campus wide total is 70 MW (operator figure), not applied to this individual building. Baxtel separately notes 9 MW of additional Tier III capacity expected campus wide from Q4 2026, a future figure not applied to critical_it_mw.

reading.body:
The Intergate Columbia A building sits on the SDC Columbia campus in East Wenatchee, one of three completed buildings within a 70 MW campuswide facility powered by hydroelectric generation at 5 cents per kilowatt-hour. The operator does not publish capacity at the building level, so the individual load hosted in this structure is not known. Campus-wide, the SDC Columbia site ranks third by published capacity in Washington state, behind only two other facilities, though 46 data centers are mapped in the state and most publish no figures.

The SDC Columbia campus is positioned as a contender in the Pacific Northwest region where Sabey operates two Washington campuses totaling published capacity of over 120 MW, plus additional capacity under construction in Virginia, Texas, and Oregon. Hydroelectric power at wholesale rates addresses one constraint on AI scaling: the cost of electricity. Whether this building or campus will be built out to serve AI training workloads at scale depends on factors not published here, including whether available capacity will be allocated to that workload and whether grid interconnection capacity to feed the campus is adequate for the AI compute densities required.

The registry tracks this facility as one of eleven Sabey rows in Washington state only, though the company operates six campuses nationally. Building-level capacity data would clarify whether Intergate Columbia A represents material supply in the AI infrastructure market or is primarily sized for other tenant profiles. A fourth building under construction at the campus, plus 9 MW of Tier III capacity expected by Q4 2026, suggests growth at the site, but forward capacity additions do not yet count as supply available to deployers today.
